## Executable scoped release-readiness gate contract — 2026-10-05

Implement this ordinary release-tooling unit under the adopted 0.3.0 plan and this issue's existing scoped-release rule. It adds no constitutional interpretation, guarantee admission, tag or publication authorization.

**Problem and result.** The current `check_constitution.py --require-release-ready` unconditionally rejects and mentions the three broader pending obligations as a blocker. Replace that placeholder with an executable, fail-closed readiness gate. A truthful scoped 0.3.0 candidate may retain the broader QS/PR/RS pending obligations. It must still satisfy every applicable 0.3.0 acceptance criterion and preserve all admitted guarantees. Source-only constitutional validation, closed Issue counts, and an arbitrary JSON `passed` field do not establish release readiness.

**Verification inputs.** Keep GitHub as the sole decisions/progress ledger. A candidate may contain an acceptance-evidence index, not a second backlog: the exact 108 selected Issue IDs and 13 groups from the approved tracker, each adopted criterion's Issue/snapshot reference and digest, implementation/Reference/migration/positive-and-negative evidence references, and its reviewed disposition. Missing or unresolved criteria fail. The index cannot invent blanket waivers, silently reduce criteria, or move work to later releases; only the already explicit later-version boundaries recorded in the Issues are eligible exclusions. Do not manufacture a completed real index while the implementation remains incomplete. Human specification review remains distinct from mechanical evidence validation; a hashed Issue snapshot does not authenticate human adequacy.

Keep generated verification receipts outside the candidate commit to avoid self-referential commit hashes. Bind the exact candidate commit/tree, product version, edition 2026, schema/profile identities, CI run/attempt, validation selection/results and actual planned artifact bytes separately. The trusted base and trusted hosted-job context are supplied by the caller/workflow, not chosen by candidate JSON. JSON must not supply arbitrary executable commands. Use fixed registered validators, reject unknown/duplicate fields and identities, and recheck mutable inputs after verification.

**Checks.** Require (1) a clean candidate identity and version synchronization, without dependency updates; (2) complete acceptance-evidence coverage; (3) ratified text/adoption identity, trusted-base guarantee continuity and actual current Lean verifier replay; (4) full validation profile AND full proof lane, with all eight required suites successful for the same commit/run/attempt; (5) successful package/source/fresh-install records and the exact expected native assets, each matching its source commit and actual bytes; (6) truthful pending-versus-admitted proof scope, production-path and migration coverage. Preserve edition, release, qrate schema, native protocol and artifact identity as separate concepts. Frontend edition validation alone cannot satisfy the outstanding effective-edition-to-native-acceptance criterion.

**CI placement and provenance.** Remove the release check from inside `check-docs`; a readiness job must run after the real validation suites, avoiding a circular dependency. Reuse the existing required-suite aggregation and add release-specific full-lane checks. Run the release gate for tags and an explicit manual readiness request; ordinary development PRs/full validation do not require all 108 issues to be finished. Receipts saved on failure are diagnostic artifacts, never proof of success. Consumers must compare actual downloaded bytes with producer digests carried by trusted same-run job outputs and check run/attempt/commit identities. Merely hashing an offline report does not authenticate GitHub CI provenance.

The legacy `--require-release-ready` entry point must delegate to this gate or reject missing required context clearly; it must never succeed from source-only checks. Existing non-release constitutional checks retain their purpose. Keep all current real missing acceptance evidence as a failure with actionable diagnostics.

**Required regression evidence.** Reject missing/duplicate Issue IDs, criterion removal, unauthorized exclusions, stale/missing evidence, a different commit or merge commit, tests/model proof lanes, skipped/cancelled/missing suites, failure-created receipts, wrong run/attempt/digest, source-only proof validation, admitted-guarantee removal, fabricated discharge, mismatched asset bytes/source/version, missing expected assets and changed inputs during checking. Include a complete small synthetic positive candidate that truthfully retains the three broader pending obligations and preserves/replays the two admitted scoped guarantees; fixture success is not actual repository readiness. Exercise CLI delegation and workflow placement/provenance, not only internal schema helpers.

Publication readback remains a distinct later action: tag peel, downloaded GitHub/registry assets and installed artifacts must match the checked candidate after separately authorized publication. This unit neither publishes nor calls a candidate “published”, and does not claim final readiness for the current unfinished tree.
